prototype: unsigned int __fastcall CalculateCrc32(const void *data, unsigned int size, unsigned int initial_crc)
short_summary: Computes the standard CRC32 checksum over a given data buffer, initializing the lookup table on first use.
detailed_summary: The function first checks a boolean flag at `byte_42285D` to see if the CRC32 lookup table has been initialized. If not, it calls `InitCrc32Table` to populate it. It then performs standard byte-by-byte CRC32 computation: it takes the initial CRC value passed via `edx` (inverting it initially with `not`), loops through the `esi` bytes starting at memory address `edi`, indexes into the lookup table `dword_422860` using the XOR combination of the current byte and the low byte of the accumulated CRC value, and finally inverts the resulting bit pattern before returning it in `eax`.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer over which the CRC32 is calculated.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the data buffer in bytes.

parameters.name: initial_crc
parameters.description: Initial CRC value (typically 0 for a fresh checksum, or a continuing value).

return_value: The computed 32-bit CRC checksum in eax.
side_effects: Initializes the global CRC32 lookup table at 0x00422860 on its first invocation by calling sub_4189C0.
